raw_responses.Bulgarian:
The chart is a line graph that illustrates the sparsity ratio of SDPA output across different layers, with a threshold of 1e-2. The graph displays three distinct data series, each representing the sparsity ratio before and after applying a gate, as well as after applying an average gate.

The x-axis is labeled "Layer" and spans from 0 to 20, with a linear scale and uniform intervals of 5 units. The y-axis is labeled "Sparsity Ratio" and ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, also with a linear scale and uniform intervals of 0.2 units.

The first data series, represented by a blue dashed line, shows the sparsity ratio before the gate. It starts at approximately 0.15 at layer 0 and decreases to around 0.01 by layer 5, remaining relatively stable thereafter, with an average sparsity ratio of 0.03.

The second data series, depicted by an orange dotted line, represents the sparsity ratio after the gate. It begins at 1.0 at layer 0 and gradually decreases to around 0.2 by layer 10, followed by fluctuations between 0.2 and 0.4 from layer 10 to 20, with an average sparsity ratio of 0.44.

The third data series, shown as a green dash-dot line, illustrates the sparsity ratio after the average gate. It starts at 1.0 at layer 0 and decreases to approximately 0.1 by layer 10, remaining relatively stable around 0.1 from layer 10 to 20, with an average sparsity ratio of 0.33.

DESCRIPTION: The line graph displays the sparsity ratio of SDPA output across 20 layers, comparing three different scenarios: before gate, after gate, and after average gate, with distinct lines and colors representing each scenario, and showing varying trends and average sparsity ratios.
